{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Gibraltar|Cuisine of Gibraltar]]

'''Torta de acelga''' (chard pie) is believed to be based on a [[Cookbook:Spinach|spinach]] pie eaten in parts of [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Italy|Italy]] and is also very similar to the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Greece|Greek]] '[[Cookbook:Spanakopita|spanakopita]]'. A very similar pie is eaten in the Ligurian Region during Easter, called Torta Pascualina. This pie is traditionally eaten on Good Friday in Gibraltar. 

==Ingredients==

* 1 small package [[Cookbook:Puff pastry|puff pastry]]
* 6 bunches of [[Cookbook:Chard|acelga]] (chard)
* 6 [[Cookbook:Egg|eggs]]
* [[Cookbook:Bread Crumb|Breadcrumbs]]
* [[Cookbook:Grater|Grated]] [[Cookbook:Cheese|cheese]]
* [[Cookbook:Parsley|Parsley]]
* 2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] [[Cookbook:Mincing|minced]] [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]]
* Seasoning to taste

==Procedure==

# Remove the stems of the acelga (these stems will become useful for another recipe called Potaje de acelga). 
# Wash the leaves very well to remove any grit or soil. [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the acelga leaves, drain really well, and [[Cookbook:Chopping|chop]] them. [[Cookbook:Frying|Fry]] them for a few minutes in hot olive oil then set aside.
# [[Cookbook:Dough#Rolling|Roll out]] the pastry and lay on an oven-proof [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|pie dish]] leaving sufficient pastry to close the pie later. 
# [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] the eggs and add all the ingredients to make a nice filling. 
# Add to the acelga and mix all together. 
# Fill the pie dish with this “relleno” or filling and close the pie with the pastry. 
# [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the oven at [[Cookbook:Oven Temperatures|150°C (300°F)]] for about 30 minutes or until the pie is nice and golden. 

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* You can boil the acelga the night before to save time.
* You can make a pastry by mixing one glass each of [[Cookbook:Olive Oil|olive oil]] and [[Cookbook:Water|water]] then adding [[Cookbook:Flour|flour]] until a soft [[Cookbook:Dough|dough]] is achieved, but this dough won't be as flaky as puff pastry.
